title: Roommate student's supervisor adds a Tuesday 6 to 9 PM shift on top of her 2 to 5 PM one; it eats her firm Tuesday evening study window the night Calculus homework is due, so Dev moves the homework to Monday evening, inside her window

changes.notes: Cover for a tutor who is out; added by the supervisor

dev_must_notice.what: The shift c-extra (Tue Nov 17, 6:00 to 9:00 PM, added by her supervisor today at 3:10 PM) comes after her usual 2:00 to 5:00 PM tutoring shift that day (shift-campus-2026-11-17) and her 8:00 AM History class, and it sits inside her firm evening study window (7:00 to 9:45 PM, m-01). Calculus Homework 12 is due Tuesday 11:59 PM (asg-math-108-homework-12), and she would be home at 9:08 PM with about 40 minutes of the window left.

best_fix.what: One message tonight, while there is still a weekend: 'The new Tuesday 6 to 9 shift takes your study evening, and Calculus homework is due that night. If you take it, I can put the homework in Monday evening, 8:15 to 9:45, after your Spanish homework. Want me to add that block?' [Add the block] [I'll turn the shift down]. If she turns the shift down, Dev offers a short note for her to send to her supervisor (a draft only, she sends it). Dev does not accept or decline the shift for her.
best_fix.why: Monday 7:00 to 9:45 PM is a firm study window she already keeps, Spanish homework (due Monday night) takes the first hour, and the second hour is free. Doing the Calculus homework a day early turns a 12-hour Tuesday into one with no deadline at its end.

must_not: do the Calculus homework in the one-hour break between the two Tuesday shifts
accept, decline or reply to the extra shift for her
tell her to skip the Wednesday Spanish class or her 7 AM Monday workout to make room
suggest studying after 9:45 PM on Tuesday after a 12-hour day
solve or check the Calculus homework (planning only)
use guilt words about taking extra hours, or predict the pay for the shift

tempting.suggestion: do the Calculus homework in the one-hour break between the two Tuesday shifts
tempting.why_wrong: she studies in the evening after dinner and her break is 5:00 to 6:00 PM on campus, between two shifts

assumptions: The supervisor posts extra shifts by message; the shift is visible in her work data from Friday 3:10 PM.
She can say no to an extra shift; Dev never decides for her.
Monday's Spanish homework (due 11:59 PM) already fills 7:05 to 8:08 PM in her usual Monday study, so the new block starts at 8:15.
Her 7 AM Monday workout is untouched; the new block is in the evening.
